To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
religion and religious behavior are positively associated with attitudes towards working mothers.
religious affiliation is positively associated with attitudes towards working mothers, and that those attitudes in turn are negatively associated with women’s labor market outcomes.
religion is positively associated with conservative attitudes toward women’s labor market behavior, and that these attitudes, in turn, have a negative impact on female labor force participation.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the role of religion for individuals’ behavior in the family sphere.
the role of religion as a determinant of attitudes and behavior in the labor market.
the relationship between religion, attitudes towards working women and female labor participation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
religion has only limited explanatory power for women’s labor market behavior.
religion is not a major determinant of attitudes towards working mothers or women’s labor market behavior.
religion matters but that it does not explain much.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
religious beliefs are important in shaping attitudes towards working mothers.
religious involvement is associated with more traditional attitudes, but these attitudes have only a small impact on labor market behavior.

religious affiliation and involvement are positively associated with attitudes towards traditional gender roles, which in turn are negatively related to female labor force participation, but only in the case of East Germany.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effect of religion on women’s labor market decisions is mediated by attitudes towards working mothers.
religious affiliation and religious participation are positively correlated with traditional attitudes towards working mothers.
religion is a relevant factor in the analysis of attitudes and behavior of individuals and that the relationship between religion, attitudes, and behavior is not straightforward.
